question.worked_solution:
First, we select the identity that contains a ${tan}^{2}⁡x$ term. So we can use the identity 

$$
1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Using the above, we compute the given integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }({cos}^{3}⁡x+{tan}^{2}⁡x{cos}^{3}⁡x)\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{cos}^{3}⁡x(1+{tan}^{2}⁡x)\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{cos}^{3}⁡x{sec}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{cos}^{3}⁡x\cdot \frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,{|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi -\operatorname{sin}⁡0 \\  & =0-0 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$
